evidence:
Row 31 (workbook Quality Checks + Internal Quality Checks row 31; skill references/quality-checks.md:131-132). Every plural/whole-collection and 'unchanged' wording in all 5 judge.toml files and the functional/polish/visual/gate prompts was walked against frozen task bytes (paths relative to .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r13/task).

WHOLE-COLLECTION WORDING (each graded over the full set, no sampled row):
- gates/constraints/judge.toml:18-23 hro_gate_shared: 'exactly one card for that candidate in Applied' -> reads the whole Applied column for duplicates.
- scored/functional/judge.toml:24 hro_job_open: all four invalid inputs (blank title, 0, 51, 2.5) plus non-manager are each required refused; protocol S (functional/prompt.md:27) runs every one.
- :33 hro_add_candidate: six J1 cards 'in the order added', and the independent context must read the same order.
- :105/:231 hro_interview_full / hro_bulk_places: places counted for the whole set; 3-into-2 refused, and 'Fails if any of the three enters'.
- :213 hro_bulk_move: full ordering Y, W, X and A2, V; 'only some move' fails.
- :222 hro_bulk_all_or_none: 'none of the set moves', with the offending card tested both first in board order (Z with V) and last but selected first (V with W, B(10a)). That defeats an implementation that validates only the first card, or only the selection-order head.
- :240 hro_undo_restores: every card (Y, W, X) back at its exact place, Applied reads Y, W, X, Z, A2, plus V unchanged.
- :249 hro_undo_conflict: the changed card is a non-first member of the move (X in V+X at B(11); W in Y+W at B(14)), which defeats an 'only checks first card' undo.
- :267 hro_activity: 'every successful board action performed on J1 and J2 before A, by any account', with 'each card of every single and multi-card move' and 'every undo', newest first, and the filter must show 'all of that job's lines and only those'. Protocol A (prompt.md:49) lists every protocol S..V.
- :276 hro_activity_refusals: 'none of the refused attempts in this review'.
- :168/:177/:186 observer/candidate/anonymous: each listed replay is required refused ('each'), not a sample.
- :330 hro_thread_earlier: 'until none remain' over Noor's 120+ seeded messages.
- :339 hro_unread_counts: per person (Lena, Rafael, Mei); count and total; 'Rafael's own messages never count'.
- :384 hro_candidate_view: 'each candidate's own applications all appear'. Seed has Noor on JOB-PLAT and JOB-DSGN, and Tomas on JOB-DATA plus the new J2 card, so 'all' is a real multi-row collection; an app showing one row fails.
- :393 hro_candidate_private: 'no response a candidate page receives', backed by prompt.md:43 'Capture every request ... inspect every response' including SSE/WebSocket frames.
- :411 hro_restart: jobs, card order per stage, notes, messages, unread counts and activity are all compared.

'UNCHANGED' GUARDS VS LEGITIMATE SIDE EFFECTS:
- The rules file says 'Adding a note does not count as a change' (rules:98-99). Protocol B(12) (prompt.md:35) adds a note to A2 and has Mei re-order a different card (Y) before Rafael's undo, which must GO AHEAD (hro_undo_conflict :249 control). So the rubric affirmatively protects the legitimate side effect rather than punishing it.
- Recomputing positions: at B(12) Screen reads Y,W,X,Z,A2, and Y can only move down (swapping with W). A2's place is untouched, so even an app that bumps versions on any positional shift is not punished.
- L-protocol undo of E: A's Offer<->Interview moves do not touch Screen.
- Golden: solution/app/src/index.js:302-318 and :354 compare per-card version_after, bumped only for moved cards (writeColumn renumbering does not bump versions). Neighbour shifts and notes do not block undo. Raw evidence qc/repairs/hireops-2026-10-03-workspace/results/workspace.json (sha verified against the index, source hashes match the frozen bytes) records 'undo ignores other cards, is blocked by a reject' passed=true. That is scripted golden evidence, not a judge run.
- Polish :18 hro_pol_live_board says scroll 'has not been reset' rather than 'unchanged', which tolerates the layout shift from the other card's move. :36 hro_pol_earlier_place allows 'within a few pixels'.
- Global 'A refused action must not change any card, order, message or note' (prompt.md:19) applies only to refused actions; an optimistic display then put back is explicitly allowed (:132 hro_refused_put_back 'or never left it').

BROKEN APP TRIED: one that validates bulk rules or undo freshness on the first card only fails hro_bulk_all_or_none (B(10a)) and hro_undo_conflict (B(11), B(14)). One that shows only a candidate's first application fails hro_candidate_view. One that logs a multi-card move as a single card fails hro_activity.

CONFORMING ALTERNATIVE TRIED: an app that bumps every positional neighbour's version on re-order is not punished at B(12), as computed above. An app logging one line per multi-card move naming each card is explicitly accepted (:267).

OBSERVATIONS (not row-31 defects; routed for the owner):
(a) hro_restart (:411) compares 'unread counts' before and after restart. Protocol D (prompt.md:51) lists 'last messages' before 'unread count', and Rafael's own conversations (Tomas J2 and Noor) are already read at the end of U, so opening them does not move the counts. A judge that records counts and then opens a still-unread seeded conversation could see a self-caused change. That is low likelihood; it is a wording note only.
(b) rules:91 'Every card must satisfy all the rules above' is graded for skip and places on bulk moves. Bulk stale-version and hiring-manager per-card stage limits on a mixed bulk are not exercised. This is a coverage question for rows 26/30, not whole-collection wording in a criterion.

No configured judge run, Oracle or model score exists (raw-evidence-index scope says so). This row is a rubric-text property and is decidable from source, so no missing measurement is waived.
